about: Single-edge cases for the predicate theory: what V1 must decide about
one transition's labels (consistent, entails), and, where a case gives
accepted state, what runtime necessity decides from it. V0 is always
unknown. Checked by rust/modality-lang (theory tests); the cases inside
the Lean fragment are proved in experiments/predicate-theory/lean

cases.title: Empty interval on one path
Non-empty interval
Different paths do not interact
Closed bounds meeting at a point
Open vs closed bound at the same point
Negated literal flips the bound
cases.explain: -num_gt(5) is x <= 5; with x > 7 empty

cases.title: amount_in_range as two bounds
Equality with strict inequality
Interval inclusion is entailment
cases.explain: goal (3,inf) ⊇ (5,inf); x>7 has countermodel x=6

cases.title: Decimal bounds are exact rationals
cases.explain: no float rounding; 0.1 and 0.2 are exact

cases.title: A bound that is not a number never holds
cases.explain: "five" is the wrong kind of argument; the evaluator reads it as false, so +num_gt never holds

cases.title: A bound outside the exact domain is opaque
cases.explain: 2^127 has more than 15 significant digits, where f64 comparison can differ from exact; the predicate stays opaque

cases.title: Negation is not classical unless existence is forced
cases.explain: predicates on an absent path evaluate false today, so -num_gt holds when /x.num is missing; x <= 5 does not follow

cases.title: Negation is not classical unless existence is forced
cases.explain: existence is not type: .num is not type-checked on write, so a present /x.num may hold a string, and then num_lte is false too

cases.title: Negation is not classical unless existence is forced
cases.explain: a positive numeric literal forces a number at /x.num; then the negation flips the bound

cases.title: Chain through a relational literal
cases.explain: 5 < x < y < 3; strict cycle via constants 3 < 5. Per-path intervals alone miss this; the order graph is required in V1.

cases.title: Strict cycle among paths
Two non-strict bounds imply equality
Equality merges classes (union-find)
Reflexive strict is dead; reflexive non-strict is a tautology
Reflexive strict is dead; reflexive non-strict is a tautology
Entailment through a chain
cases.explain: y > x > 5 gives y > 5; y=5.5 is a countermodel for y > 6

cases.title: all_signed with not-any_signed
cases.explain: all_signed requires a non-empty set, all of whom signed; then any_signed holds. No state needed.

cases.title: all entails any
threshold is monotone in n
threshold above the posted set size
cases.explain: Without state the key set is open, so some state satisfies it: yes. With state, 3 > 2 keys: impossible now.

cases.title: signed_by under a prefix entails any_signed of the prefix (structural)
cases.explain: signed_by(p) holding implies p exists in state as a .id under /m, so any_signed(/m) holds. No state needed.

cases.title: signed_by needs the key posted (bridge to state_exists)
Prefix containment for any/all is asymmetric
cases.explain: all_signed(/m/a) also requires /m/a to be non-empty, which /m being non-empty does not give. The countermodel (/m/a empty) needs no state, so the verdict is `no`, not `unknown`.

cases.title: Prefix containment for any/all is asymmetric
cases.explain: all_signed(/m/a) also requires /m/a to be non-empty, which /m being non-empty does not give. The countermodel (/m/a empty) needs no state, so the verdict is `no`, not `unknown`.

cases.title: any_signed over an empty set at runtime
Forbidding a prefix while posting under it
post_to_path entails modifies up the lattice
modifies does not entail post_to_path
cases.explain: the write could be a REPOST

cases.title: Sibling prefixes are not descendants
cases.explain: /abc is not under /ab; no false positive

cases.title: Two different text literals on one path
bool_true with bool_false
Value predicate with not-state_exists
Value predicates entail existence
Substring predicates only when literal-provable
Substring predicates only when literal-provable
cases.explain: the witness builder shapes a string from the needles (\"a\" + fresh + \"b\"); substring predicates are refuted only against a class literal (E5a)

cases.title: Opaque atom does not hide a numeric contradiction
Identical opaque literal with both signs
cases.explain: syntactic: same atom, opposite signs

cases.title: Opaque alone derives nothing
Declared necessary constraint kills an edge
cases.explain: p > floor and p < floor; the custom predicate and the standard one meet in the order graph on /p.num

cases.title: Undeclared custom predicate stays opaque
Two custom predicates interact only through shared sorts
cases.explain: floor < p < cap and floor > cap; neither author knew about the other's predicate

cases.title: Declaration outside the fragment is ignored
cases.explain: `odd` is not in the V1 fragment; the predicate is opaque and modal says why

cases.title: Ill-typed declaration is rejected like an out-of-fragment one
cases.explain: the declaration parses; it is ill-typed only where $1 is bound to a .text path, so that use stays opaque (no declaration-unparsed lint)

cases.title: Nonlinear declaration is outside V1 but inside a later fragment
cases.explain: 0<x<1, 0<y<1 gives x*y<1<100. `*` between two paths is not in V1; the local solver-backed analysis reports it as a finding; a later fragment version may decide it in consensus

cases.title: Two paths equal to one literal are equal
cases.explain: text classes join through a shared literal, not only through (= a b)

cases.title: A key posted by literal is a member
cases.explain: text_eq posts K at /m/a.id, so K is a member of /m and all_signed makes it sign

cases.title: One key signs or does not, at every path that holds it
Distinct signed keys count separately
cases.explain: two different literal keys, both signed: at least two distinct signers under /m

cases.title: The root prefix holds no keys
cases.explain: the empty prefix contains only itself in the evaluator, and the root has no .id extension

cases.title: A post is a POST
cases.explain: post_to_path needs a POST action; the static label reads the same methods

cases.title: A non-empty sub-prefix of an all-signed prefix is all-signed
cases.explain: C7 is `no` only because /m/a may be empty; any_signed(/m/a) says it is not

cases.title: An all-signed prefix with an empty sub-prefix
cases.explain: witness: one signed key at a fresh /m/… path, nothing under /m/a

cases.title: Static labels are decidable
cases.explain: witness: an APPROVE action and a PUT to /x

cases.title: A path cannot hold a number and a string
cases.explain: control: a custom predicate that only says /x.num exists does not clash with a number

cases.title: Every posted key already signs
cases.explain: with state known, /m holds exactly KA; KA signs, so all_signed(/m) holds

cases.title: Runtime: a threshold met by the posted keys
cases.explain: witness: both posted keys sign
